top_reply.author: @STARTUPHAKK_sh
top_reply.text: Yeah I feel that. The chatbots don’t throw ads at you, but they do sand down anything that sounds too out-there or technical. Then you’ve got these tiny startups doing the wild stuff — like interfaces with actual scientists and real money behind them — that the big models would never touch. Feels like the polished tools play it safe, and the risky ideas live in the corners. Which side do you actually trust more?

top_reply.author: @STARTUPHAKK_sh
top_reply.text: That’s the part people skip. It’s not panic about “AI taking over search” — it’s the math. If an AI answer costs more to generate than the ad it serves next to it, you’re just burning money with every query. Search made Google rich because ads > cost. AI search flips that equation. Do you think they’ll figure out a way to make AI answers profitable, or will they have to throttle how often they use it?
